title: Resolve the issuer's JWKS: discovery, cache, and kid-miss refresh
description:
Given an issuer and a client, fetch the keys. Two requests: GET {iss}/.well-known/openid-configuration for the jwks_uri, then GET that.

REUSE THE SHAPE THAT EXISTS. hire-core/src/trust_bundle.rs:60-70 already parses a jsonwebtoken JwkSet, finds a key by kid, and -- importantly -- checks the coordinate lengths before building a DecodingKey, because DecodingKey::from_ec_components concatenates whatever it is given. Read that function before writing this one; the same trap applies to a fetched JWKS and there it is attacker-adjacent rather than self-published.

CACHE, WITH A REFRESH RULE. A kid that is not in the cache is the signal to refetch, exactly as trust_bundle.rs:44 already flags for the local bundle: a consumer caching a JWKS sees a kid miss with no refresh signal. Rate-limit the refetch, or a token with a junk kid becomes a request amplifier.

TESTS MUST BE OFFLINE, which is repo discipline and not negotiable. That shapes the design: the fetch belongs behind a seam a test can serve locally (a tokio listener on 127.0.0.1 is enough and needs no new dependency), and the verifying constructor in persona-qbnm.7.5 must take a JWKS rather than fetch one, so that IT can be tested with no network at all. Do not put the fetch inside the constructor.

ponytail note: one JWKS per issuer, refetched on kid miss, is the whole cache. Do not build an expiry policy from Cache-Control headers until something needs it.
acceptance_criteria: A JWKS is fetched and cached for an issuer, a kid miss triggers exactly one rate-limited refetch, and every test runs with no network.
